name: Packaged food and FMCG brands

problems.words: I only see primary sales, I don't know what actually sold in the market
quick_ideas: Ask your largest distributors for secondary sales and stock once, so you see the gap
Use one simple format for all, so their numbers can be compared.

workzap_build.text: a weekly form where every distributor would submit secondary sales and stock in one format, feeding one owner summary.

problems.ask_first: Do any distributors send secondary sales now?
problems.free_stops: The website and data format distributors use are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one distributor's sell-in with the same week's retailer reorders, so you see where stock is not moving onward.
Give one staff member a weekly notebook for distributor stock and market offtake notes, so follow-up happens from one place.

problems.words: Expired stock comes back from the market and we eat the cost
quick_ideas: List near-expiry stock at your factory and top distributors, so you can move it before it returns
Note which SKUs come back most, so production of those is reviewed.

workzap_build.text: a near-expiry radar showing stock by batch and expiry at the factory and distributors, with alerts.

problems.free_stops: The expiry tracking and action rules are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count returned expired cases by sku and by distributor for one recent cycle, so the worst repeat pockets stand out.
Make one person update a single near-expiry list every week, so stock gets discussed before it comes back.

problems.words: Distributor claims for schemes take months, and I'm not sure schemes reach the retailer
quick_ideas: List every open claim with its date and amount, so the oldest are cleared first
Ask for evidence with each claim, so verification isn't starting from zero.

workzap_build.text: a scheme and claim tracker with rules, evidence, approval status and ageing.

problems.ask_first: How long do claims usually take to settle?
problems.free_stops: The claim evidence rules and approval flow stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare claimed scheme outlets with one sales beat's recent shop feedback, so you see whether the scheme reached retailers.
Give one person a fixed weekly hour to review open claims in one notebook, so approvals stop drifting between desks.

problems.words: Order bookers fake visits, shops say nobody came
quick_ideas: Call a few shops on a beat to confirm visits, so you see whether there's a real gap
Review each booker's orders by shop, because missing shops show quickly.

workzap_build.text: an order booker phone tool with a beat plan, shop check-in with location and photo during work hours, order capture and visit history, with bookers told how it works.

problems.ask_first: How do you know bookers visited their shops now?
problems.free_stops: The beat plan and check-in rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each order booker's claimed shop calls with that day's actual orders from those shops, so fake visits show up fast.
Give one supervisor the daily job of noting missed shops in one place, so every handover starts with the same exceptions.

problems.words: Some SKUs always out of stock in the market, others rot, and production is on gut feel
quick_ideas: Compare last month's production with secondary sales by SKU, so you see what's over- and under-made
Note the SKUs that run out most.

workzap_build.text: a weekly production plan built from recent secondary sales and current stock.

problems.ask_first: How do you decide what to produce each week?
problems.free_stops: The planning logic is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one recent production run by sku with the same period's market offtake and returns, so gut-feel planning gets challenged.
Give one planner a fixed weekly slot to update one sku shortage and surplus list, so production talks start from facts.

problems.words: Packaging film and cartons run out and the line stops
quick_ideas: List each raw and packaging material with its supplier lead time, so you know when to order
Check stock of the ones that stopped the line before.

workzap_build.text: raw and packaging stock with reorder points tied to supplier lead times, with alerts.

problems.free_stops: The reorder points per material stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which packaging items stopped the line in the past few weeks, so the repeat troublemakers are clear.
Give one store staff member one notebook for packaging lows checked at the same time daily, so reordering gets noticed earlier.

problems.words: I don't know margin by SKU after schemes and returns
quick_ideas: Work out the margin on your top SKUs once including schemes, returns and freight, so the real picture shows

workzap_build.text: a SKU margin view including schemes, returns, freight and listing fees, refreshed every month.

problems.ask_first: Which SKUs do you think make the least?
problems.free_stops: The margin model is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare two high-volume skus after returns, freight and schemes from one recent period, so the weaker earner becomes obvious.
Give one person one page per sku to note all give-aways and returns weekly, so real profitability is reviewed consistently.

problems.words: Supermarkets pay late and deduct for returns
quick_ideas: List every unpaid invoice by supermarket with its age, so you chase the oldest first
Match deductions to returns notes, so disputes have evidence.

workzap_build.text: a modern-trade receivables tracker with invoice ageing and deductions.

problems.ask_first: How long do supermarkets usually take to pay?
problems.free_stops: The tracking and dispute steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each supermarket's unpaid invoices with its return deductions for one recent period, so the biggest holdbacks are clear.
Give one person a fixed weekly slot to update one unpaid invoice list, so follow-up stays active with each account.

problems.words: Batch on the shelf has a defect and I can't trace which line or shift
quick_ideas: Note line, shift and date for every batch, so a complaint can be traced
Check that QC is recorded at the time on every shift, so each batch can be traced when a question comes.

workzap_build.text: batch traceability from raw material lot to line, shift and dispatch, with a QC checklist on a tablet.

problems.ask_first: If a complaint comes in now, can you trace the batch?
problems.free_stops: The traceability set-up is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Check a few recent complaint packs against batch notes from that day, so missing line or shift details show immediately.
Give one shift lead the job of keeping batch, line and shift notes in one register, so complaints can be traced faster.

never_say: Anything about food registration, labelling, nutrition claims, halal certification or authority approvals.
Recall steps — point to the authority and qualified advisers.
Advice on distributor contracts, exclusivity or competition law.
Help with price-fixing, under-invoicing or relabelling expired stock.
That sales or margins will improve by any amount.

sample_reply.person: We sell through 14 distributors. I see what I sell to them, but no clue what they sell to shops. Need a solution before Ramadan.
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be brought under control, and none of it needs special equipment.
First, ask your largest distributors for secondary sales and godown stock once, so you see the size of the gap before Ramadan.
Second, give them all one simple format, so their numbers can be compared.
A lasting version would be: with a shared form where every distributor submits sales and stock weekly in one format, feeding a simple view of stock in the market by SKU and city.

Shall I get a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
